items.gist: The secret Kula ritual is taught for qualified practitioners, with guru-disciple transmission and the siddha krama's superior efficacy.
Kula is Śakti and related powers; seeing all beings thus, the vīra's mind-speech-body actions constitute Kula worship.
Kulejyā is sixfold and not dependent on external ritual items; the Kaula is six-maṇḍala-free and covering-free.
Forbidden substances are used after vāmāmṛta purification; wine is Śiva-rasa and grape wine is supreme, to be drunk always.
Arghapātra, yāgadhāma, and dīpa are the three essentials; argha is Śakti-saṃgama and dīpa is cows, requiring attentive practice.
The practitioner enters the yāgakuṭa, purifies, and prepares initiation and mantras before transforming substances into nectar.
The arghapātra is filled and identified with Bhairava; one satisfies oneself and then worships externally.
Maṇḍala sizes and materials are specified, and the worship procedure begins with Gaṇeśa.
Gaṇeśa, vaṭuka, gurus, siddhas, yoginīs, and pīṭhas are worshipped in the siddhacakra arrangement.
Sādhikāra deities, mudrās, pīṭhas, and ūrdhvaretas are enumerated, with virya's non-dispersal defining the latter.
Gurus' wives and mālinī are treated specially, then the mantracakra and kuleśvarī are worshipped.
Raśmi groups, directional deities, and aṣṭakas are worshipped in the prescribed order.
Pīṭha and kṣetra worship is performed, with pīṭhas nyāsa'd in the body from head to throat.
